== Biography ==

The Hatter is a resident of Wonderland, known to be mad. He is celebrated for the tea parties he holds beneath a tree, where conversation turns upon questions of language and logic with surprising rigour. When it is suggested that to say "I mean what I say" is the same thing as saying "I see what I eat," the Hatter objects with great certainty: "Not the same thing a bit! You might just as well say that 'I see what I eat' is the same thing as 'I eat what I see'!" He speaks of Time as one might speak of an acquaintance—as someone one might converse with—and holds in contempt those who claim never to have spoken with Time.

The Hatter finds himself later in the King's court, summoned to give evidence at trial. There, beneath the Queen's unwavering stare, he becomes greatly agitated, trembling so violently that his shoes fall away. When the King presses him to remember what transpired, the Hatter confesses himself a poor man, quite unable to recollect the particulars. In his distress, he drops his teacup and bread-and-butter, falling to one knee before the throne.

== Relationships ==

'''[[March Hare]]''' — strained friendship. They share a residence in Wonderland and host the mad tea party together, though their association seems marked by tension.

'''[[Queen]]''' — enemy. The Queen called for the Hatter's head after he sang at the tea party, and at trial her intense stare causes him profound distress and visible fear.

'''[[Alice]]''' — acquaintance. Alice joins the Hatter at his tea party, engaging in philosophical discourse with him about the nature of language and meaning.

'''[[Dormouse]]''' — acquaintance. The Dormouse attends the Hatter's tea party as a third guest.

'''[[King]]''' — adversary. The King interrogates the Hatter at trial, demanding evidence and threatening him with execution if his memory fails.
